title: Past Simple: Negatives and Questions
summary: Say what did not happen in the past and ask questions about completed actions. Use did and did not with the base verb and give short past-tense answers.
learningObjectives: Make negative past simple sentences with did not and didn't.
Form yes/no past simple questions using did before the subject.
Form information questions with a question word, did and the base verb.
Use the base verb after did or did not, including irregular verbs.
Give correct positive and negative short answers with did or did not.

explanation.heading: Use did not or didn't for past negatives
explanation.body: To say an action did not happen, use did not (usually didn't) before the base verb. This pattern is the same for all subjects. Say I didn't travel, she didn't call and they didn't leave. Did already shows the past, so the main verb does not have a past ending.
explanation.example: We didn't visit the museum on Wednesday.

explanation.heading: Start past yes/no questions with did
explanation.body: Put did before the subject, then use the base verb: Did + subject + base verb? Use this pattern with I, you, he, she, it, we and they. Even when the affirmative past verb is irregular, the question uses the base form: She took a photo becomes Did she take a photo?
explanation.example: Did your uncle bring his camera yesterday?

explanation.heading: Put question words before did
explanation.body: For information questions, place where, what, when, why or how before did + subject + base verb. Do not put did after the subject. For example, ask Where did they stay? rather than Where they did stay?

explanation.heading: Compare the affirmative, negative and question forms
explanation.body: Use the past form only in an ordinary affirmative sentence: They went home. Negatives use didn't go, and questions use Did they go? The same rule applies to regular verbs: We watched, we didn't watch, did we watch? Past questions and negatives of be use was/were instead (Unit 10).
explanation.example: Nina bought the tickets, but she didn't buy any snacks.

explanation.heading: Give short answers with did or didn't
explanation.body: For yes/no questions beginning with did, answer Yes, I did; Yes, he did; No, we didn't; or No, she didn't. The short answer uses did or didn't, not do or does, because the question asks about the past.
explanation.example: Did the shop close early? Yes, it did.

comparisons.title: One past event in three forms

left.label: Affirmative past
left.note: Made is the irregular past form in an affirmative statement.

right.label: Negative past
right.example: Mira didn't make a cake yesterday.
right.note: Didn't carries the past meaning; make stays in its base form.

left.label: Present simple
left.example: Does Oliver usually walk to work?
left.note: Does is for a regular present habit.

right.label: Past simple
right.example: Did Oliver walk to work yesterday?
right.note: Did asks about a finished event; the main verb is still walk.

examples.sentence: I didn't hear the alarm this morning.
examples.note: Didn't is followed by the base verb hear, not heard.

examples.sentence: Did Hana finish the puzzle last night?
examples.note: Did starts a past question; finish remains in the base form.

examples.sentence: Where did the visitors park their car?
examples.note: Where comes before did + subject + base verb.

examples.sentence: We didn't have enough time on Sunday.
examples.note: The past negative of have uses didn't have.

examples.sentence: Did the children enjoy the game? No, they didn't.
examples.note: The negative short answer repeats didn't with they.

commonMistakes.incorrect: She didn't saw the final episode.
commonMistakes.correct: She didn't see the final episode.
commonMistakes.why: After didn't, use the base verb see, not the past form saw.

commonMistakes.incorrect: Did you went to the festival?
commonMistakes.correct: Did you go to the festival?
commonMistakes.why: Did already indicates the past, so use the base verb go.
In a direct past question, did comes before the subject.

commonMistakes.incorrect: In reply to 'Did they win?': No, they don't.
commonMistakes.correct: In reply to 'Did they win?': No, they didn't.
commonMistakes.why: The question uses did, so its negative short answer uses didn't rather than don't.

studyTips: After did or didn't, ask yourself whether the following verb is in its base form.
Practise each past statement in three forms: They arrived. They didn't arrive. Did they arrive?
For information questions, remember the order: question word + did + subject + base verb.

exercises.prompt: ___ you see the stars last night?
exercises.feedback: Last night refers to the past, so the question begins with Did.

exercises.prompt: We stayed at home yesterday; we ___ visit the museum.
exercises.feedback: A negative past action needs didn't + the base verb visit.

exercises.prompt: Choose the correct question about a trip last week.
choices: Where did Mia go last week?
Where Mia did go last week?
Where did Mia went last week?
exercises.feedback: The order is where + did + Mia + the base verb go.

exercises.prompt: Choose the correct short answer to: "Did your cousins phone yesterday?"
exercises.feedback: Did questions take short answers with did or didn't; Yes, they did is affirmative.

exercises.prompt: Complete with one word: They stayed outside because they ___ have a ticket for the concert.
acceptedAnswers: didn't
exercises.feedback: They stayed outside because they did not have a ticket; didn't is followed by the base verb have.

exercises.prompt: Complete with one word: Where ___ your family travel last summer?
acceptedAnswers: did
exercises.feedback: Last summer refers to the past, so a question uses did.

exercises.prompt: Complete with the base form of take: Did Ava ___ a photo at the museum?
acceptedAnswers: take
exercises.feedback: After did, use the base form take, not took.

exercises.prompt: Complete the short answer with one word: "Did the film start late?" "Yes, it ___."
acceptedAnswers: did
exercises.feedback: A positive short answer to Did it ...? is Yes, it did.

exercises.prompt: Correct the sentence: She didn't saw the final episode.
acceptedAnswers: She didn't see the final episode.
She did not see the final episode.
exercises.feedback: The verb after didn't is the base form see.

exercises.prompt: Correct the question: Did your uncle drove home last night?
acceptedAnswers: Did your uncle drive home last night?
exercises.feedback: A did question uses the base verb drive, not drove.

exercises.prompt: Correct the question: Where you did find that book?
acceptedAnswers: Where did you find that book?
exercises.feedback: Put did before the subject you.

exercises.prompt: Correct the reply to "Did they finish the project yesterday?": No, they don't.
acceptedAnswers: No, they didn't.
No, they did not.
exercises.feedback: Use didn't for a negative short answer about a past action.

speakingExercises.prompt: Say a complete negative past sentence using: Nia / not / cook / dinner / yesterday.
acceptedAnswers: Nia didn't cook dinner yesterday.
Nia did not cook dinner yesterday.
speakingExercises.feedback: With didn't or did not, use the base verb cook.

speakingExercises.prompt: Ask a complete past question using: when / your train / arrive / yesterday.
acceptedAnswers: When did your train arrive yesterday?
speakingExercises.feedback: Put when first, followed by did + your train + arrive.

speakingExercises.prompt: Give a negative short answer to: "Did the twins buy flowers?"
acceptedAnswers: No, they didn't.
No, they did not.
speakingExercises.feedback: A past negative short answer with they uses didn't.

speakingExercises.prompt: Say one complete negative past simple sentence beginning with 'The children'. Use: not / bring / umbrellas / yesterday.
acceptedAnswers: The children didn't bring umbrellas yesterday.
The children did not bring umbrellas yesterday.
speakingExercises.feedback: Use didn't or did not followed by bring, not brought, in a past negative.

speakingExercises.prompt: Change this past statement into a negative sentence; keep all the other information: I saw the message on Monday.
acceptedAnswers: I didn't see the message on Monday.
I did not see the message on Monday.
speakingExercises.feedback: After didn't or did not, use the base verb see instead of saw.

speakingExercises.prompt: Someone asks, 'Did Mara find the missing folder yesterday?' Give a positive short answer using 'she' and no extra information.
acceptedAnswers: Yes, she did.
speakingExercises.feedback: A positive short answer to Did she ...? is Yes, she did.

speakingExercises.prompt: Correct only the verb form in this question and say the complete corrected question: Why did the guests left early?
acceptedAnswers: Why did the guests leave early?
speakingExercises.feedback: After did, use the base form leave, not the past form left.

speakingExercises.prompt: Report what happened in ONE sentence starting with 'Last Sunday' and linking the two facts with 'but': we / not / see / the main exhibition; we / see / the garden.
acceptedAnswers: Last Sunday, we didn't see the main exhibition, but we saw the garden.
Last Sunday, we did not see the main exhibition, but we saw the garden.
speakingExercises.feedback: Use didn't see for the negative and saw for the affirmative completed action.

listeningExercises.audioText: Did you finish the book yesterday evening?
listeningExercises.prompt: What does the speaker ask about?
listeningExercises.feedback: Did you finish asks whether the listener completed the book at a past time.

listeningExercises.audioText: No, he didn't. He stayed at home on Saturday.
listeningExercises.prompt: Which short answer do you hear?
listeningExercises.feedback: Didn't makes the reply a negative answer about a past event.

listeningExercises.audioText: Where did the children play after school?
listeningExercises.prompt: Type the one-word past question auxiliary you hear.
acceptedAnswers: did
listeningExercises.feedback: Did comes before the subject in past simple questions.

listeningExercises.audioText: I didn't buy the blue jacket because it was too expensive.
listeningExercises.prompt: What did the speaker decide about the jacket?
choices: They bought it for a friend
They decided not to purchase it
They returned it after wearing it
listeningExercises.feedback: Didn't buy means the purchase did not happen, because the price was too high.

listeningExercises.audioText: Did Aisha send the email on Tuesday? No, she didn't. She sent it on Wednesday.
listeningExercises.prompt: On which day was the email sent?
listeningExercises.feedback: The answer rejects Tuesday and says the message was sent on Wednesday.

listeningExercises.audioText: Did Liam call the doctor? No, he didn't. He sent a message instead.
listeningExercises.prompt: How did Liam contact the doctor?
listeningExercises.feedback: He did not call; he contacted the doctor by message instead.

listeningExercises.audioText: Our neighbours didn't use the lift after the power cut.
listeningExercises.prompt: Type the one-word contracted past negative helper immediately before 'use'.
acceptedAnswers: didn't
listeningExercises.feedback: Didn't is short for did not and comes before the base verb use.

listeningExercises.audioText: Did your cousin take the early train on Friday?
listeningExercises.prompt: Type the one-word base verb immediately after 'your cousin'.
acceptedAnswers: take
listeningExercises.feedback: The past question uses did followed by the base verb take, not took.
